heading: John 1:19–51: the Baptist and the first disciples
lede: Four scenes: John the Baptist questioned by envoys from Jerusalem, his testimony about Jesus, the first disciples, and the call of Philip and Nathanael. For each verse: which Greek manuscripts up to AD 900 preserve it, where they disagree, and which early Latin manuscripts carry it.
latin_note: Latin evidence matters twice in these verses: three Old Latin manuscripts support “the Chosen One” at 1:34, and three support “hereafter” at 1:51.

verses.translation: This is the testimony of John, when the Jews sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to ask him, “Who are you?”
He confessed and did not deny it; he confessed, “I am not the Messiah.”
They asked him, “What then? Are you Elijah?” He said, “I am not.” “Are you the prophet?” He answered, “No.”
So they said to him, “Who are you? Let us give an answer to those who sent us. What do you say about yourself?”
He said, “I am the voice of one crying out in the wilderness, ‘Make straight the way of the Lord,’ as the prophet Isaiah said.”
They had been sent from the Pharisees.
They asked him, “Why then are you baptizing, if you are neither the Messiah, nor Elijah, nor the prophet?”
John answered them, “I baptize with water. Among you stands one whom you do not know,
the one coming after me; I am not worthy to untie the strap of his sandal.”
This took place in Bethany across the Jordan, where John was baptizing.
verses.greek_where_variant: ἐν Βηθανίᾳ ἐγένετο πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου

verses.translation: The next day he saw Jesus coming toward him and said, “Look, the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world!
This is the one of whom I said, ‘After me comes a man who ranks ahead of me, because he was before me.’
I myself did not know him, but I came baptizing with water so that he might be revealed to Israel.”
And John testified, “I saw the Spirit coming down like a dove from heaven, and it remained on him.
I myself did not know him, but the one who sent me to baptize with water said to me, ‘The one on whom you see the Spirit come down and remain is the one who baptizes with the Holy Spirit.’
And I myself have seen and have testified that this is the Son of God.”
verses.greek_where_variant: οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ

verses.translation: The next day John was again standing there with two of his disciples,
and watching Jesus walk by, he said, “Look, the Lamb of God!”
The two disciples heard him say this, and they followed Jesus.
Jesus turned, saw them following, and said to them, “What are you looking for?” They said to him, “Rabbi” (which translated means Teacher), “where are you staying?”
He said to them, “Come and see.” They came and saw where he was staying, and they stayed with him that day. It was about the tenth hour.
One of the two who heard John speak and followed him was Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother.
He first found his own brother Simon and said to him, “We have found the Messiah” (which is translated Anointed).
verses.greek_where_variant: εὑρίσκει οὗτος πρῶτον τὸν ἀδελφὸν τὸν ἴδιον Σίμωνα

verses.translation: He brought him to Jesus. Jesus looked at him and said, “You are Simon son of John. You will be called Cephas” (which is translated Peter).
verses.greek_where_variant: σὺ εἶ Σίμων ὁ υἱὸς Ἰωάννου

verses.translation: The next day he decided to go to Galilee. He found Philip and said to him, “Follow me.”
Philip was from Bethsaida, the town of Andrew and Peter.
Philip found Nathanael and said to him, “We have found the one Moses wrote about in the law, and the prophets also: Jesus son of Joseph, from Nazareth.”
Nathanael said to him, “Can anything good come out of Nazareth?” Philip said to him, “Come and see.”
Jesus saw Nathanael coming toward him and said of him, “Here is truly an Israelite in whom there is no deceit!”
Nathanael said to him, “Where do you know me from?” Jesus answered, “Before Philip called you, when you were under the fig tree, I saw you.”
Nathanael answered him, “Rabbi, you are the Son of God! You are the King of Israel!”
Jesus answered, “Do you believe because I told you I saw you under the fig tree? You will see greater things than these.”
And he said to him, “Truly, truly, I tell you, you will see heaven opened and the angels of God going up and coming down on the Son of Man.”

variants.label: Son / Chosen One
variants.title: “The Son of God” or “the Chosen One of God”?

readings.witnesses: 𝔓5 (probably, from the space available) · 𝔓106 (probably) · 01 (first hand) · Old Latin b, e, ff2 (first hand) · Old Syriac (Sinaitic and Curetonian)

variants.explanation: The most interesting variant in this section, and one where new discoveries changed the picture. “Son of God” has the numbers and the great codices. “Chosen One” has fewer witnesses, but they are early and widespread: the first hand of Sinaiticus, Old Latin and Old Syriac, and two 3rd-century Oxyrhynchus papyri, one of them (𝔓106) only published in the late 1990s. Some witnesses combine the two as “the chosen Son”. Scholars who favour “Chosen One” argue that a scribe would more easily change it to the familiar “Son of God” than the reverse, and that John the Baptist here echoes Isaiah 42:1. Ehrman sees the change to “Son” as part of 2nd-century debates about Christ’s status; Quek accepts “Chosen One” as original but finds that explanation unnecessary. The Nestle–Aland text prints “Son”; some recent translations (the NET Bible, for example) print “Chosen One”.

variants.label: Bethany / Bethabara
variants.title: Bethany or Bethabara?

readings.witnesses: 𝔓59 (probably) · 𝔓66 · 𝔓75 · 02 · 03 · 04 (first hand) · 019 · 032 (replacement quire) · 037 · 038 · 044 (first hand) · most Latin · Bohairic Coptic
01 (a later corrector) · 04 (corrector) · 017 · 029 · 044 (corrector) · 083 · many later manuscripts · Sahidic Coptic · Origen

variants.explanation: The earliest manuscripts say Bethany, which is not the village near Jerusalem but a place “across the Jordan”. In the 3rd century Origen, visiting the region, could find no Bethany beyond the Jordan and was shown a place called Bethabara associated with John’s baptism; he adopted that name in his Commentary on John (book 6), and his reading spread into later manuscripts and eventually into the King James Version. A case where a named scholar’s field research, not a scribe’s slip, changed the text.

variants.label: John / Jonah
variants.title: “Son of John” or “son of Jonah”?

readings.witnesses: 𝔓66 · 𝔓75 · 𝔓106 · 01 · 03 (first hand) · 019 · minuscule 33 · Old Latin · Coptic

variants.explanation: Matthew 16:17 calls Peter “Simon Bar-Jona”. The later reading in John brings the two Gospels into line, a common kind of scribal change (harmonisation). The KJV follows the later text (“Simon the son of Jona”); most modern translations read “son of John”.

variants.label: first
variants.title: Who found Simon “first”?

readings.english: he first (the first thing he did was to find his brother)
he was the first (to find his brother)

variants.explanation: A one-letter difference. With πρῶτος, Andrew is the first of the two disciples to find his brother, which hints that the unnamed second disciple later found his own brother too. A few Old Latin manuscripts are reported to read “in the morning” instead (to check). Small in itself, but it shapes how readers identify the unnamed disciple.

variants.label: hereafter
variants.title: “Hereafter you will see”?

readings.witnesses: 02 · 017 · 021 · 030 · 034 · 037 · 038 · 044 · most later manuscripts · Old Latin e, q, r1 · Peshitta Syriac

variants.explanation: The KJV’s “Hereafter ye shall see” comes from the later reading. The phrase probably came in from Matthew 26:64 (“from now on you will see the Son of Man”), another harmonisation. The four earliest witnesses lack it.

translation_sweep.question: What time is “the tenth hour”?
translation_sweep.explanation: Counting hours from sunrise, as was usual in the ancient Mediterranean, the tenth hour is about 4 p.m., which is how several modern translations render it. A minority view holds that John counts from midnight, which would make it 10 a.m. The manuscripts do not settle this; it will be treated with other time references in John (4:6, 19:14) in the translation sweep.
